correctness.rationale: For odd N, choose a cyclic start so two alternate gaps a,c are less than N/2 (at most one of four gaps can exceed half). The exact paired-phasor identity gives squared modulus as 4[(cos alpha-cos gamma)^2+2cos alpha cos gamma(1-cos delta)]. If a != c, strict concavity and monotonicity force (a,c)=(1,2); if a=c, odd parity forces b != d and a<=(N-3)/2, giving the same exact bound through 4 sin(3pi/(2N))sin(pi/(2N)). Equality gives the unique gap orbit. For even N, a vanishing sum of four unit vectors is exactly two antipodal pairs. Primitive multiplication permutes residues. Python CHECK.py independently tested 80,730 four-subsets at N=4..26; the proof, not the experiment, covers all N.

value.rationale: A natural binary four-site mask requires distinct phase atoms, unlike unrestricted sparse root sums. The restriction changes the sharp primitive Fourier near-cancellation floor from asymptotically pi^2/N^2 to 3pi^2/N^2 at every odd order and yields a single exact extremal translation orbit, while even orders admit zero through two antipodal pairs. This is a complete, motivated all-order quantitative classification relevant to finite spectral-mask stability, with clear limits to four equal-weight sites.
